name: Obambo — Additional Material (d20pfsrd)
body:
More on Obambo from d20pfsrd.com.

These sections appear on d20pfsrd.com's page "Obambo" but are not part of the Obambo entry, which is unchanged.

Treasure standard

An obambo (or ‘forsaken one’) is a ghost of the wild tropics, a spirit birthed from ancient tribal wisdom now lost and forgotten, swallowed up in death in the jungle’s embrace.

With neither grave to bind him to home nor funerary rites to speed him to the afterlife, the embittered spirit instead seeps into the ground, the roots of plants, and the crawling things beneath, becoming as one with the jungle itself.

Obambos are cunning, spiteful, and treacherous, but they yet remember their old role of teacher and storyteller, a duty and an obligation they both love and loathe. While dealing with them is dangerous, obambos are known to assist those in need, if they can meet the obambo’s price.

An obambo may rise when a tribal elder or shaman perishes in the wild and is never properly laid to rest. Without the proper rites to lead the spirit to the afterlife, the obambo is lost and sundered from his community and tribe, cursed to wander the wild. If an obambo’s home can be discovered and its remains returned for proper burial (usually in a small house-like shrine on the land of a blood relative), its spirit could be laid to rest forever, but few obambos ever find such peace. Instead, whispered memories drive the obambo to meander endlessly between jungle villages, all vaguely familiar but none ever seeming right. Many who meet an obambo do not realize it is a phantom spirit, for they look alive, if ancient; however, their appearance is changed in death, and even those who once knew them (if not already long dead) no longer recognize them. Obambos may be male or female.

Obambos are solitary wanderers of bush and veldt. Animals shy away from them, but obambos share a keen spiritual symbiosis with vermin and plant life. Through the obambo’s journeys, these are his audience, attending faithfully to the obambo’s endless tales and treating him as a wise mentor and leader. Their obeisance, however, can never satisfy the obambo’s yearning for the rapt attention of his own kind to his riddles, stories, and lessons. An obambo is easily angered by the foolish, however, and its stern reproofs often leave their pupils as drooling husks or mindless insectile drones. An obambo’s plant or vermin sycophants have been known to devour such hapless wretches, or even to ravage entire villages as they sit enthralled by the obambo’s tales. As long as a few remain and learn from the obambo’s teaching, it is satisfied. In any case, an angry obambo hardly needs assistance in the act of destruction, as an obambo’s spiritual communion with the land enables it to merge itself into the land, rising up as a roaring titan melded of soil, mud, vegetation, and crawling vermin.

Obambo’s Favor

Obambos often establish a reputation as darkling oracles, wise and knowledgeable about the jungle, its creatures, and its people. Obambos create small shrines to themselves called akinfa, usually in hollow trees where supplicants may bring gifts and the obambo may sit within. These gifts may be of material wealth, but as a teacher the obambo prefers gifts that show the talents of the supplicant, be it a crafted item, a song, a story, a riddle, or some other performance.

An obambo begins any meeting as unfriendly, but a supplicant may make a Craft or Perform check opposed by the obambo’s Appraise skill to offer a gift they have made (offering a magical or masterwork item grants a +2 circumstance bonus to this check). If they succeed, the obambo is impressed with their skill and its attitude becomes indifferent. If the check fails, the obambo remains unfriendly, and if failed by 10 or more the obambo is insulted and becomes hostile. If a creature offers an item they did not personally create, the obambo is entitled to a Sense Motive against their Craft or Perform DC; if it succeeds, it automatically becomes hostile.

An obambo is unaffected by Diplomacy until it receives a suitable gift.

An indifferent obambo’s attitude may be improved with Diplomacy or by offering additional gifts as above; each gift that pleases the obambo improves its attitude by one step.

Using Intimidate against the obambo makes it immediately hostile, as does any unsuccessful Bluff attempt. An obambo can also be challenged to a storytelling contest as an opposed Perform (oratory) check; if the PC wins, the obambo is truly impressed and immediately becomes helpful.

Each time a supplicant tries to influence the obambo’s attitude beyond indifferent, the obambo will respond with a question or riddle, using its Bluff skill or one of its Knowledge skills; a supplicant must oppose the check with the same skill. Each time a supplicant fails this check, the obambo becomes annoyed and all skill checks to influence him suffer a -2 cumulative circumstance penalty for 1 hour.

An indifferent obambo will answer questions in riddles, requiring a Sense Motive check opposing the obambo’s Bluff check to understand the answer. An obambo made friendly will speak more plainly, granting a +10 bonus to Sense Motive checks to understand its riddling speech. It may also offer goodberries to supplicants who have offered it additional gifts. A helpful obambo will answer questions plainly and may also agree to use one of its spell-like abilities to aid the supplicant. However, an obambo expects gratitude and an additional gift after it lends its aid. If no gift is forthcoming, or if another favor is requested by the same person, the obambo flies into a rage at the ingratitude and attacks.
